rules.description: The primary dark ink used for all foundational typography, main UI elements, and inverted sections to ground the design.
when_to_use: Body typography, headings, and inline link underlines
Primary CTA button backgrounds and borders
Footer and cookie consent banner backgrounds
Animated Lottie logo paths and mobile menu icons

rules.description: A suite of warm, print-inspired off-whites that serve as the foundational background for the site, creating an editorial, academic feel.
when_to_use: Primary page, mobile menu, and dropdown menu backgrounds
Primary text and icon color in the dark footer and Fable CTA section
'Oat' background fills for the release package banners
Subtle borders separating nav items and dropdown content

rules.description: A muted gray used strictly for secondary information and subdued links within dark-themed areas to ensure they don't compete with primary content.
when_to_use: Footer copyright text and secondary links
Social media icon fills in the footer
Description text and secondary links in the cookie consent banner

rules.description: A purely structural black used to establish base fallbacks and build layered drop-shadows.
when_to_use: Low-opacity layered box-shadows on navigation dropdowns
Root HTML tag fallback text color
Fallback text colors on video source tags

rules.description: A deep charcoal used to create subtle contrast and visual separation against the primary Ink Black background.
when_to_use: Backgrounds for individual toggle panels within the cookie consent banner
Divider border on the dark 'Try Claude' combo button

insights: The palette eschews vibrant brand colors entirely, relying on a stark, high-contrast, editorial combination of warm ivory paper and ink black to project academic seriousness, safety, and transparency.
Dark mode inversion is used strategically to create visual impact for major product announcements (like Fable and Mythos) and to anchor the footer, without needing to introduce new accent colors.
Depth and structure are handled with extreme subtlety—using very low opacity blacks for shadows and tinted blacks for borders—to maintain a flat, print-like aesthetic across the interface.
